about: Lane MENUWORK-1: what RotWK 2.01 does when each menu control is pressed, for tools/menus/menu_inventory.py. Rows are matched in order by a regular expression on the control's path (the Apt button's target path, or a gadget's placeholder name) and optionally on the screen name; the first match wins. 'source' cites the RotWK address or the decompile file (and whether it is an inference). 'expect': 'nothing' = retail's press has no effect either; 'unavailable' = retail greys it out. 'effect': the control's intended effect as checks (tools/menus/menu_inventory.py); 'retail_unhandled': commands the movie sends that retail's engine has no handler for either (not a defect). 'owner': another lane owns the defect.

controls.note: the HUD's side command bar teardown callback (a game.dat name) has no handler: an in-game HUD gap, not this button's. Lane MENUFIX-2: the restart's load is synchronous, so the walk can sample the stack after the new game is up (Palantir.apt before and after): the restart request the host carries out counts too; AptGameLoading::OnInitialized has no handler in the binary (AptSimpleScreens.h). Lane MENUFIX-3: the restart drops the HUD screen (AptPalantir and its command registrations) before the Palantir movie's clips run their unload actions, so PalantirCommandUI::OnButtonFrameUnloaded (ported, RW 0x930200), OnToggleFlashUnloaded and OnSubMenuUnloaded (RW 0x930340, registered with OnSubMenuLoaded RW 0x93023D in RW 0x930A25) arrive with no screen: the frame / submenu slots they drop went with it (the port keeps no submenu slots: OnSubMenuLoaded is not ported, ControlBar.cpp). Nothing is left to release; the teardown order is a follow-up, not this button's
